title: Arc Length and Radian-to-Degree Conversions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Convert theta = 3*pi/4 radians to degrees, and calculate the arc length s subtended by this angle along the circumference of a circle with radius r = 8 cm.

steps.title: Convert Radians to Degrees
steps.explanation: Multiply the angle in radians by the standard conversion factor 180 degrees per pi radians. The pi symbols cancel, leaving the degree measure.
steps.why: Conversion ratio between radians and degrees derived from 2*pi rad = 360 degrees.

steps.title: Apply the Arc Length Formula
steps.explanation: Substitute the radius r = 8 cm and the angle theta = 3*pi/4 radians directly into the circular arc length formula s = r*theta.
steps.why: Arc length equals radius multiplied by angle strictly when angle is measured in radians.

steps.title: State the Numerical and Exact Results
steps.explanation: State the exact expression in terms of pi and compute the decimal approximation.
steps.why: Standard mathematical reporting gives exact analytic answers with decimal context.
